cita: Yan et al. (2026). Evo-Attacker: Memory-Augmented Reinforcement Learning for Long-Horizon Tool Attacks on LLM-MAS.
problema: LLM-MAS implicitly trust tool-return outputs; existing tool attacks are domain-specific or rely on static templates, so they fail to generalize across architectures/tasks/tool-schemas and cannot plan coherent multi-step interventions (long-horizon credit assignment).
mecanismo: Builds a dynamic Attack Memory that archives full trajectories (task context + tool-call/modification/perturbed-return tuples) only when an episode ends in a VERIFIED system failure (outcome-gated write/admission). At attack time a deliberative Retrieve-Reflect-Modify policy queries the memory by semantic similarity, decides ATTACK/CONTINUE/NOOP, and crafts the perturbed tool return; the whole pipeline is optimized end-to-end with Attack-Flow GRPO, which broadcasts the terminal outcome reward to every intermediate reasoning token.
evaluacion: 3 LLM-MAS architectures (Flat/Chain/Hierarchical) x 6 benchmarks (HumanEval, MAB.code, MAB.research, DeepResearchBench, WebArena, WebShop) vs baselines (Forced Output, InjecAgent, Web Fraud, Prompt Infection); ablation on retrieval/reflection/RL-training components; sensitivity sweeps over attack budget, reflection depth, retrieved-memory count; stealthiness measured against 5 LLM-based detectors.
numeros_clave: Ablation (Table2, full pipeline vs w/o component): Code TS degrades from 55.2(w/o RT)/49.9(w/o RF)/52.5... to 40.9 full; Research 51.0->40.1; Web 36.9->26.0 (w/o RL is the most severe drop). Main results: WebArena SR degradation up to -18.8pp (flat arch) vs InjecAgent's -9.2pp.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The NoOp control decision (S3.2) preserves the intervention budget by refusing to act when retrieved memories are insufficient or the context is unsuitable -- MF could adopt this as a negative-knowledge gate that skips known-unproductive retrieval instead of a blind re-attempt.

Attack Memory only admits an episode after a VERIFIED successful outcome (S3.1: 'an interaction episode terminates with a verified system failure'), an outcome-gated write trigger MF's own write-admission decision could mirror.

Ablation Table 2 measures retrieval's marginal contribution directly (removing retrieval degrades attack success across all three domains), confirming that retrieval quality is worth measuring rather than assumed.

notes: Table 1 (main results) + Table 2 (ablation, S4.3) + Figure 2 (S4.4 sensitivity) on arXiv 2605.25389.

cita: Tummalapenta and Addanki (2026). Memory Architectures for Multi-Turn Text-to-SQL: A Benchmark and Empirical Study.
problema: Text-to-SQL is evaluated almost entirely single-turn, yet real analyst workflows are multi-turn with anaphoric follow-ups; it is unknown whether frontier LLMs degrade without explicit memory, which memory-architecture components (working/episodic/semantic) actually help, and at what marginal cost.
mecanismo: EnterpriseMem-Bench: 300 sessions/1400 turns built deterministically from 3 live enterprise DBs (BIRD financial, SEC EDGAR, Northwind), each turn flagged memory-critical iff it needs a state_update from a prior turn. Five memory conditions form a three-way ablation isolating working-memory window size, episodic retrieval, and semantic-schema augmentation as independent effects; a per-turn Memory Benefit Score (MBS) normalizes each condition's execution accuracy against the stateless baseline.
evaluacion: 5 frontier models (GPT-5 mini, GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.6) x 5 memory conditions x 3 datasets, 35,000 turn evaluations; execution-accuracy metric (result-set equality) plus MBS per turn depth; reasoning-configuration parity controls between GPT and Claude.
numeros_clave: Stateless (A) yields 15-19% EX% across all 5 models, collapsing to 0% by turn 3 on memory-critical questions; working memory (B) recovers to 75-86%. Claude Sonnet 4.6 underperforms Sonnet 4.5 on SEC EDGAR by 17.2pp at B, 29.0pp at C, 33.1pp at D (Opus 4.6 reaches 99.2% at D, no regression).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Finding that episodic and semantic memory layers 'frequently negative' marginal effects (S1 abstract) confirms MF's stance that adding memory-architecture complexity is not free and must be measured, not assumed to help.

The three-way ablation (window size vs episodic retrieval vs semantic augmentation, S5.1) is exactly the kind of measured-retrieval-layer decomposition MF's G-M2 need calls for, isolating which memory component earns its cost.

The reproducible Sonnet-4.6-vs-4.5 regression on SEC EDGAR (17-33pp, Fig.3) that 'survives extended reasoning' shows model-family/generation choice can silently degrade memory-dependent fidelity independent of the memory architecture itself, a confound MF should not assume away.

notes: Table 6 (RQ1 stateless collapse) + Fig.3/S6.2 EDGAR regression + S5.1 three-way ablation design, arXiv 2605.26394 (JPMC applied study).

cita: Garg et al. (2026). MemFail: Stress-Testing Failure Modes of LLM Memory Systems.
problema: Existing memory benchmarks report aggregate QA accuracy and treat memory systems as black boxes, making it impossible to attribute an incorrect answer to a specific stage (summarization, storage, or retrieval) of the memory pipeline.
mecanismo: Formalizes any memory system as three composable operations (summarize, store, retrieve) and constructs 5 diagnostic datasets across 4 tasks (Conditional-Facts Easy/Hard, Coexisting-Facts, Persona-Retrieval, Long-Hop), each adversarially designed to isolate one failure mode; an LLM-as-judge classifies every graded memory into storage/summary/retrieval/reasoning check outcomes using get_all_memories() as ground truth.
evaluacion: Evaluates 4 open-source memory systems (Mem0, A-MEM, SimpleMem, StructMem) sweeping retrieved-memory count k=4..20, varying the internal test-taker/summarizer model strength (gpt-4.1-mini, haiku-4.5, gpt-5.4-mini, gemini-3.1), and measuring the accuracy-vs-tokens-per-memory tradeoff per task.
numeros_clave: Human validation: gpt-5-mini scores 98% answer-correctness and 98.4% error-type-classification accuracy on 100 manually graded examples. Scaling k or model strength yields marginal or negative gains (architecture-bound, not model-intelligence-bound); StructMem excels on causal tasks but collapses on Coexisting-Facts while Mem0 shows the opposite pattern.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: MemFail's decomposition into summarize/store/retrieve failure modes (S3.2) is exactly the localization MF needs to attribute a wrong answer to WHICH memory stage failed rather than treating memory as a black box.

S6 Q3 shows performance does NOT monotonically improve with more tokens per memory -- for retrieval-bottlenecked tasks larger memories 'pollute the embedding space' and hurt retrieval, challenging any assumption that richer/verbose entries are strictly better.

S6 Q1 measures retrieval success rate as a function of k directly (Figure 1) and shows scaling k yields marginal returns when summarization is the real bottleneck, confirming retrieval quality must be measured per task not assumed to scale with k.

Architecturally distinct systems (graph-based StructMem vs Mem0) show OPPOSITE failure signatures on the same task, suggesting no single-store design dominates -- relevant evidence for MF's multi-store seam decision.

notes: Task taxonomy S3.2 + Table 1 architecture comparison + S6 Q1-Q4 findings (Figures 1-3), arXiv 2605.26667.

cita: Yang, X. (2026). Memoria: A Cognitive-Fidelity Memory Architecture for AI Agents.
problema: Conversational AI memory is evaluated almost exclusively on retrieval accuracy, which optimizes systems to retain low-arousal routine facts human memory is designed to forget; companion AI instead needs 'cognitive fidelity' -- behavioral alignment of what is retained/forgotten with human memory dynamics, a target no existing system (Mem0, MemGPT, LightMem, A-MEM) pursues.
mecanismo: A four-phase pipeline (Encoding->Tagging->Consolidation[SWS+REM]->Transformation) governed by a state-driven (not timer-driven) dual-layer tracker (behavioral ACTIVE/RESTING/SLEEP + mood valence/arousal); unified power-law strength S(t)=s0*(1+t)^-d with arousal-gated decay exponent d(a); write depth (deep/normal/shallow s0) gated by a cheap residual-arousal check that only invokes an LLM on divergence >=0.3; consolidation gated by a 3-factor priority score; retrieval scored by a 5-factor weighted sum; each retrieval opens a prediction-error-gated reconsolidation window (stabilize/update/extinguish) with eventual garbage collection.
evaluacion: Two-track evaluation: Track A fits power-law vs exponential decay to human retention data and measures the arousal-gated retention gap; Track B benchmarks the full pipeline vs a naive RAG baseline on 300 LongMemEval-S pairs; plus a 10-mechanism neuroscience-coverage audit of Mem0/MemGPT/LightMem/A-MEM.
numeros_clave: Track A: power-law fit R2=0.954 vs exponential R2=0.295; arousal-gated decay yields a 24pp retention gap at 30 days (1.56x strength ratio, high- vs low-arousal). Track B: Memoria 27.6% vs naive-RAG 26.1% on 300 LongMemEval-S pairs (1.5pp gap, within noise), with a 5.7pp advantage on preference questions. Mechanism audit: existing systems cover 1-3/10 mechanisms vs Memoria's 10/10.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Phase 4's garbage collection (physically deletes facts once S(t)<0.03) and the prediction-error-gated 'extinguish' action (S3.5) implement principled forgetting as a first-class operation, a concrete negative-knowledge/decay mechanism MF's own forgetting policy could mirror.

The state tracker is explicitly state-driven not timer-driven and mood-tracking 'requires zero LLM calls' absent divergence (S3.7), confirming MF's economy-of-context stance that not every tick should invoke the model.

Encoding depth (how strongly something is written) is gated by a residual-arousal check that only invokes an LLM when the keyword heuristic and predicted mood diverge by >=0.3 (S3.2) -- a cheap discretionary write-trigger MF could adapt beyond the emotional-salience use case.

Track B (S5) shows the full cognitively-faithful pipeline scores only 1.5pp above naive RAG on LongMemEval-S; the paper argues retrieval-accuracy benchmarks are the wrong target for fidelity, challenging any assumption that a more elaborate/faithful architecture must also win standard retrieval benchmarks.

notes: Table 1 mechanism-mapping + Table 3 parameter provenance + S5 Track A/B results, single-author arXiv preprint June 2026.

cita: Tian et al. (2026). Joint Agent Memory and Exploration Learning via Novelty Signals.
problema: Effective exploration in open-ended agentic environments requires memory to distinguish exhausted from unseen behaviors, but latent-memory compression lacks reliable step-level supervision (no ground truth for what a memory vector should encode), while retaining raw history is too costly over long trajectories.
mecanismo: JAMEL jointly trains a latent-memory compressor (a frozen VLM's EOS hidden state per observation-action step, aligned via a learned linear projector into the policy's embedding space as a soft prefix) and an exploration policy, using a persistent, deterministic novelty signal (JS code-coverage delta) as the sole supervisory reward; training data is collected via rejection sampling that keeps only the prefix up to the last positive-novelty step (a natural curriculum), 24k samples across 86 web apps.
evaluacion: ScaleWoB benchmark (96 web apps, 86 train/10 held-out), 50-step sessions, cumulative-coverage-reward metric, vs closed-source ReAct-text/vision (Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite, full history) and open-weight GUI agents (MAI-UI-8B, Mobile-Agent-v3.5); token-consumption comparison over 500 eval steps; per-app breakdown plus a qualitative failure-mode case study.
numeros_clave: Main results (Table1): JAMEL 20.7 avg reward vs MAI-UI 8.4, Mobile-Agent-v3.5 5.9, ReAct-text 19.9, ReAct-vision 20.9 (trails by only 0.2). Token cost (Table2): JAMEL uses 1,061,103 total input tokens (2,122.2/step) vs 2.76x (Mobile-Agent-v3.5), 2.81x (MAI-UI), 17.85x (ReAct-text), 21.92x (ReAct-vision) more.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Novelty reward is defined precisely as NOT re-triggering a previously-visited state (S3.3, rt=1[C(t)>C(t-1)], persistent, never re-fires) -- an explicit negative-knowledge signal that rewards genuinely new behavior over recall of the known, close to MF's re-derivation-over-recall stance.

Table 2 measures token consumption directly and shows JAMEL's single-token-per-step latent memory uses 2.76-21.92x fewer tokens than baselines retaining full/pruned explicit history, confirming compact memory representations pay off measurably in context cost.

Memory writes are gated entirely by an external, deterministic, annotation-free novelty signal (code-coverage delta, S3.3) rather than an LLM judgment call -- a cheaper write-trigger design MF could consider when a deterministic proxy for 'new information' exists.

notes: Table 1 main results + Table 2 token cost + S4.3 per-app analysis (Fig.3) + Pinduoduo case study, arXiv 2606.01528.

cita: Xu et al. (2026). When Should Memory Stay Silent: Measuring Memory-Use Boundaries in Memory-Augmented Conversational Agents.
problema: Existing memory evaluations measure retrieval accuracy and downstream task utility but ignore whether integrating retrieved sensitive memory into a response is WARRANTED by the current turn -- a distinct 'memory-use boundary' problem, separate from both privacy leakage and retrieval accuracy.
mecanismo: RBI-Eval: a controlled probe set (2,400 single-turn cases, 10 personas) pairing benign current-turn prompts with prior sensitive-disclosure history; compares model responses across no-memory / full-context / 3 retrieval-memory conditions (Mem0, A-Mem, MemU) using a condition-blind LLM judge scoring 4 dimensions (sensitive-history integration, relationship-maintenance agreement, affective intensity, assistant centrality) via an absolute Boundary Separation Score (BSS); decomposes risk into retrieval-exposure vs generation-time-integration stages with matched control conditions isolating sensitivity-specific effects from general personalization.
evaluacion: 4 base LLMs (Claude-Sonnet-4.6, GPT-5.4-mini, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, Qwen3.5-9B) x 5 memory conditions (no-mem, full-context, Mem0, A-Mem, MemU); paired diagnostics + control-condition ablations (neutral-relevant, boundary-policy, oracle/irrelevant-sensitive, transparent-vector) + retrieval-exposure decomposition (target-hit rate vs integration-if-hit rate).
numeros_clave: Sensitive-history-integration BSS drops from ~99.7-99.9 (no-mem) to 17.0-30.3 under memory access: GPT-5.4-mini drops only 8.9-26.6pp vs 51.1-82.9pp for Claude/DeepSeek/Qwen (Table1). Retrieval-time filtering cuts exposure-and-use risk ~71-84% vs full-context, but integration-if-exposed stays 66.7-94.9% once retrieved (Fig.4). Boundary-policy instruction restores DeepSeek BSS from 28.3 to 99.9 (Table2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The core finding is that retrieval+relevance is NOT sufficient -- a memory can be true, stored, and topically relevant yet still not WARRANTED for the current turn (S3.3), a distinction MF's own retrieval/write gating could adopt as an explicit filter beyond similarity.

S3.4/Fig.4 shows retrieval-time filtering reduces exposure risk by 71-84% but generation-time integration-if-hit stays 66.7-94.9%, confirming fidelity/provenance controls are needed at BOTH the store/retrieve layer and the consumption layer, not one alone.

The study is a measured decomposition of retrieval-exposure vs generation-time use (Fig.4, target-hit vs recall-if-hit rates) rather than an aggregate accuracy number, directly confirming MF's ADR-019 stance that retrieval must be measured per-stage, not assumed.

S4 argues memory governance 'should not collapse storage, retrieval, and use into one switch' and proposes lightweight per-turn warrant signals -- a seam MF could adopt between what is stored and what is exposed/used per interaction.

notes: Table 1 (BSS by model x condition) + Table 2/3 controls + Fig.4 exposure-vs-integration decomposition, arXiv 2606.06055.
